summary: Home with a record: {the returner} is out, and {the host} has to say whether there is a room and who tells the child.
realLife: One life: He came home in 1999 after seven years for weapons and drug charges. She runs a group that prepares former inmates for work. She sent him to a fast-food job where he became a manager, and she stayed with him after he lost it. Another: After eight months in a city jail, with no one to pick him up, he took the train to his uncle's home. Years later he works at a group that helps people leaving jail and fears his record touches everything, including how his young son sees him. Another: A father came home after almost twelve years away, when his son was a high school senior. He said he had played no part in the son's success, and the two now work on the present. Another: A mother left when her daughter was four and decided in prison to be a better mother. Later she founded a group with transitional housing for women leaving prison, after working at another Baltimore group.
